title: F puts a video full screen, and the full screen shortcut it lists works
goal: Watching a video, pressing F should fill the screen with it (and F or Escape bring it back), the way video players work, instead of switching to the editor. The Full Screen button's tooltip names a shortcut, Control Command F, that does nothing today; it should work everywhere, and the tooltip should name F.
notes:
User's words: "the video's fullscreen feature lists ctrl-cmd-f as the shortcut but that does not work. and it's a bad shortcut. i expected 'f' to just fullscreen it but it puts it into edit mode".

From code reading (not run): the watch view's Full Screen transport button calls hostWindow?.toggleFullScreen and advertises .panelHelp("Full screen (⌃⌘F)") (TimelineDock.swift:1457-1467, only while editorState.isWatching). No menu row carries ⌃⌘F or toggleFullScreen (no 'Enter Full Screen' in EditorCommands.swift or the app's commands; the pro menu bar rearrangement likely dropped the system item), so the shortcut does nothing. F is the Frame tool's key (PhotonzCore/Tools.swift:106); picking a tool from the watch view brings the editor in. K is the Lens tool (Tools.swift:96). Double click on the canvas already toggles full screen (CanvasPointerDrags.swift:36). Memory rule: default to Photoshop's keys; that is why the editor question goes to a card, not a silent remap.
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults: open a recording in the watch view, press F, press Control Command F, use the transport's Full Screen button; record what each does in the audit

In the watch view, F toggles full screen for that window (picture, transport and nothing else, as the button does today); Escape also leaves full screen; F does NOT switch to the editor or pick a tool there
View > Enter Full Screen / Exit Full Screen exists in the menu bar with Control Command F (the macOS standard), in both the watch view and the editor, for image and video documents, and works
The transport button's tooltip says Full Screen (F)

In the editor, F stays the Frame tool. If the person should get F for full screen there too (Photoshop's F cycles screen modes, and its Frame tool is K, which Photonz uses for Lens), raise it as a decision card with the key moves spelled out in the option labels rather than deciding it here
Entering and leaving full screen keeps the playhead and play state; during full screen playback the menu bar and controls hide and show the way QuickTime's do
A walk opens a recording to watch, presses F, checks the window is full screen and still playing, presses Escape, checks it is back
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Reproduced at Next defaults (probe walk, front): F in the player -> Edit mode with the Frame tool ('f taken by timeline', expectTimeline: Edit mode, frame in hand). Control Command F -> 'taken by responder chain', nothing happened; View menu (menus step) had no full screen row at all. AppKit's own row, if any, would sit in SwiftUI's built-in View, which MenuBarArranger hides on the pro menu bar.

Adversarial review: a QuickTime/YouTube user expects F and Escape; a Premiere user gets full screen from the Mac's own Control Command F; F in the editor stays Frame (Photoshop parity question goes to a card on f-in-the-editor-the-frame-tool-or-full-screen). Risks found while building: macOS drops a toggle asked for mid-slide (F twice quickly left it full screen) -> the latest ask is kept and carried out a turn after the slide lands; the walk's plain wait returns before the slide ends (it happens outside the app) -> full screen waits use onTheClock.

Built: PhotonzCore/PlayerFullScreen.swift (keys, menu words, tuck-away rule; PlayerFullScreenTests), EditorState+FullScreen.swift (toggle, will/did notices, 5 Hz pointer look only while full screen, NSCursor hidden until moved), View > Enter/Exit Full Screen on Control Command F (pro menu bar), transport tip 'Full Screen (F)' and exit arrows while full screen, expectTimeline fullScreen/controlsTucked claims. Walk f-puts-a-video-full-screen-walk green; every-command-in-the-menu-bar, pro-menu-bar, menu-checkmarks, view-mode-and-edit-mode, the-menu-bar-stays-still-while-playing walks green.
